checklist: Verify your contractor license is current and valid in FL
Confirm your liability insurance is active (certificate is conditional only when the listed condition applies at permit office)
Have the property address and legal parcel number ready
Know the project value/cost — required on most permit applications

Confirm the required license is active and matches the application: Licensed Florida solar/electrical contractor or licensed general contractor with the proper scope pulls the permit — the contractor license number must appear on the application. For the service upgrade and PV electrical work, the EC/CAC/CBC license classification must match the scope; the contractor pulls the permit on behalf of the owner.
Bring 2 copies of all documents to Orange County Building Division

common_mistakes: Submitting the solar permit without structural calculations for the warehouse roof — commercial rooftop systems often get held for roof load verification
Missing required fire access pathways and roof setbacks — panels cannot cover the full roof and inspectors will fail the job if clear access routes are blocked
Assuming permit approval means the system can be energized — utility permission to operate is separate and must be obtained before turn-on
Incorrect NEC 690 labeling on disconnects, combiner boxes, and conduits — missing labels are a common final inspection failure

Submitting permit application without verifying current contractor registration status — an expired or lapsed city registration will block your application silently. Verify your registration is current BEFORE submitting.

pro_tips: Start the utility interconnection application the same day you submit the permit — utility PTO often takes longer than city review
Have the roof attachment details and structural calcs ready up front; that is the fastest way to avoid a plan review correction cycle on commercial solar
Check your Orlando/Orange County contractor registration renewal date before starting any permit application — registration lapses are the #1 avoidable rejection reason
Prepare NEC 690 labels before final inspection so the inspector can verify them without a return trip

response_body.zoning_hoa_flag: Solar jobs can be delayed by HOA CC&Rs, historic district review, or zoning overlays. For a warehouse in Orlando, verify whether the site is in a historic district, scenic corridor, or other overlay that could affect rooftop equipment visibility or placement. HOA restrictions may still limit panel placement or screening even where solar is allowed. Check local zoning and any preservation review before permit submittal.
